cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Helpful Culprit
cards.instruction: Hide that the problem is your fault while enthusiastically helping investigate it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll organize the vase investigation. Let's start with that open window; you can tell me which way the wind was blowing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I saw your elbow knock it off the table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent, a witness. You describe the elbow movement and I'll reconstruct the space. We won't need you to guess about the wind.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your elbow only moved because you reached for the biscuits.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you place the biscuit tin. I'll stand wherever you say and measure the gap. We should find out who left such a narrow route to the food.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 leads inquiry toward window; A3 accepts B witness and yields reconstruction facts; A5 lets B place tin and A body while shifting blame to layout. Confident helper authority depends on B continuing participation.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2 elbow evidence to abandon wind; A5 uses B4 biscuit motive for a controlled gap reconstruction instead of acknowledging fault.

relationship.evidence: B2 directly witnessed the knock and B4 explains reach, plausible observer correcting evasive inquiry.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns B4 causal action into enthusiastic layout measurement and displaced blame, developing the same investigation.

specificity.evidence: A1 vase/table/window and B4 biscuits establish concrete movement; guilt is now supported by witness, not mere repair residue.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 narrow route to food is self-serving interpretation grounded by B reaching fact.
